why: Appends rows via Sheets batchUpdate to a table the caller already owns/can access; the table_id/spreadsheet_id are resource identifiers sent straight to Google's API, not interpreted locally.
message_ids/label ids are forwarded to Gmail's batchModify endpoint and a verification read-back; no local interpretation of the ids occurs.
The requests list is passed through to Docs API batchUpdate; the server never interprets or executes the operations locally, Google's Docs backend does.
requests list forwarded to Forms API batchUpdate on the caller's own form; no local sink.
requests list forwarded to Slides API batchUpdate; no local interpretation.
Searches Drive by name and reads permissions via the Drive API; read-only, no injection surface.
file_id/new_name/parent_folder_id are passed to Drive's files.copy; Google enforces access on the caller's own credentials.
summary/description become the body of a Calendar API calendars.insert call; no local sink.
title/content become the body of a Docs API documents.create call; no local sink.

fileUrl supports file:// and http(s)://; file:// paths are checked by core.utils.validate_file_path (resolves symlinks, allow-lists only the attachment storage dir plus ALLOWED_FILE_DIRS, blocks .env/.ssh/.aws/credentials patterns) before any read, and http(s) URLs go through core/http_utils.py's SSRF-safe fetch (DNS-pinned, redirect-revalidated, private/loopback ranges rejected via ipaddress.is_global). base64_content is size-capped and, for zip-container formats, checked for zip-bomb ratios in _decode_base64_upload.
folder_name/parent_folder_id become the body of files.create with folder mimeType; no local sink.
title becomes the body of a Forms API forms.create call; no local sink.
title becomes the body of a Slides API presentations.create call; no local sink.
emoji_unicode/message_id forwarded to Chat API reactions.create; no local sink.
title forwarded to Apps Script API projects.create; no local sink.
sheet_name/source_sheet_name forwarded to Sheets API batchUpdate (addSheet/duplicateSheet); no local sink.
title forwarded to Sheets API spreadsheets.create; no local sink.
index/data are assembled into Docs API batchUpdate requests by docs_tables.py/table_operation_manager.py; Google's Docs backend applies them, no local interpretation.
script_id/description forwarded to Apps Script API versions.create on the caller's own project; no local sink.
Only argument is user_google_email; the returned module/source-file paths come from inspect.getsourcefile on the server's own code, not from caller input.
Reads and reports existing table geometry via the Docs API; no write, no injection surface.
script_id forwarded to Drive API files.delete for the caller's own Apps Script project file; Google enforces ownership/ACL.

filename/content_type come from Google's own attachment metadata (not directly caller-controlled beyond selecting message_id/attachment_index); bytes are saved via core.attachment_storage.save_attachment_bytes, which sanitizes the filename (strips path separators, reserved names) and writes under a UUID-suffixed name inside the fixed STORAGE_DIR.

Attachment 'path' entries are resolved through core.utils.validate_file_path before being opened, restricting reads to the allow-listed attachment/base directories; body/header strings are stripped of CR/LF before being placed into email headers.
document_id/pdf_filename/folder_id direct a Docs export + Drive upload entirely through the Google API; the PDF bytes are held in memory (io.BytesIO) and never written to local disk.
find_text/replace_text become a Docs API ReplaceAllTextRequest; matching/replacement is done by Google's backend, not locally.
Range/color/number-format arguments become a Sheets API batchUpdate request; no local sink.

trigger_type/function_name/schedule are only interpolated into a code snippet returned as advice text to the caller; the server never executes or stores this code (Apps Script triggers cannot be created via API, which is exactly why this tool exists).
resource_name is passed to the People API get; read-only.
resource_name is passed to the People API contactGroups.get; read-only.
Renders a Google Doc's own structure to Markdown via the Docs API; read-only, no local file/command sink.
Fetches Docs/Drive content via the API and returns text; read-only, no local sink.

For Office XML (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx) it parses via core.utils.extract_office_xml_text, which explicitly uses defusedxml.ElementTree (imported as ET) rather than stdlib ElementTree, closing the XXE/entity-expansion path; PDF text goes through pypdf. Declared Drive size is checked against WORKSPACE_MCP_MAX_FILE_BYTES before download.

Downloads stream to a NamedTemporaryFile then move into attachment storage via save_attachment_from_path, which sanitizes the destination filename derived from the Drive file's own name; no caller-supplied local path is ever opened for writing.
file_id passed to Drive permissions.list; read-only.
file_id passed to Drive files.get for its webViewLink; read-only.
query/time_min/time_max/event_id are Calendar API parameters sent as-is to Google's events.list/get; Google's own query parser is the 'sink', scoped to the caller's calendars.
form_id passed to Forms API forms.get; read-only.
form_id/response_id passed to Forms API forms.responses.get; read-only.

Saved via core.attachment_storage (save_attachment_bytes/save_attachment_from_path), which sanitizes filenames and writes under the fixed STORAGE_DIR with a UUID-derived name; message_id/attachment_id only select which Gmail attachment is fetched.

When exporting the full message to disk (full=True), the save uses storage.save_attachment_bytes with a filename built from subject[:80]+extension, which core.attachment_storage.sanitize_attachment_filename strips of path separators/control characters before use.

function_name/parameters are forwarded verbatim to Apps Script API scripts.run on the caller's own already-deployed script project; running a function via this API is exactly the tool's advertised purpose, and Google enforces that the script belongs to the authenticated caller.

script_id/files (source code) are forwarded to Apps Script API projects.updateContent on the caller's own project; writing arbitrary code to one's own script project is the tool's advertised purpose and Google scopes it to the caller's ownership.
